The characteristic clinical features of stiff-person syndrome include an insidious onset of stiffness and painful spasms, mostly with axial and proximal involvement, sometimes triggered by tactile stimuli, emotional stress or voluntary contraction. Spasms may be accompanied by both severe pain and autonomic paroxysms (hypertension, tachycardia and diaphoresis) that can even lead to sudden death. There may also be hyperekplexia.

extractions.value: The diagnosis of stiff-person syndrome is clinical (stiffness and painful muscle spasms) supported by electrophysiology studies (continuous motor unit activity in agonist and antagonist muscles) and exclusion of other feasible causes. Additional minor criteria are the specific autoantibodies and the response to benzodiazepines.
